study.question: Does a centered between-block ordinal/value moment supply information missing from the incumbent compressed history representation, beyond a matched-width duplicate-information channel, and does its click benefit depend on task-specific residual routing?
study.hypothesis: The incumbent sums local block summaries without exposing block identity to the scorer or adapter. In evaluation its history representation is invariant to permuting whole ten-event blocks, including the associated fields, actions and masks. Round12 supplies preliminary support for within-block order (position_task AUC 0.6635245221 versus scrambled_task 0.6630152951), but leaves this coarser invariance untouched. A separate count-centered block-rank/value moment should preserve coarse changes in history composition while retaining match and local ordinal detail. If that information is useful, block_task should exceed duplicate_task and the incumbent; task conditioning is complementary only if the factorial interaction is positive and subsequently repeated. This tests one implementation and input-ordinal information, not elapsed time or a new general temporal theory.

nearest_work.difference: Direct inherited implementation. Retain its match and local ordinal moments; append one third, globally centered block-rank/value moment rather than changing its scorer or replacing its useful local summary. Prior duplicate-information control defeated an explicit feedback-interaction detail channel. Reuse the principle that extra width alone needs a control, now by copying the retained local ordinal moment into the third channel at the same coefficient norm.

study.proposed_difference: Append a third width-112 summary. Let m[b,j] be the history mask, l[b,j]=m[b,j]*(j/9 - mean_valid_j_in_block(j/9)), and q[b,j]=m[b,j]*(b/9 - event-weighted_global_mean(b/9)). The ordinal channel uses q*sqrt(sum(l^2)/max(sum(q^2),1e-12)), gated to zero when sum(q^2)<=1e-12. The duplicate control uses l with the same gate. Contract the selected coefficients with the inherited item/action values and divide by sqrt(max(total_valid,1)), exactly as for the other moments. Both build both systems and contract three channels. Append this summary to each residual adapter input; detach it on auxiliary item-owned paths. Cross ordinal/duplicate with task/shared adapter routing. Four standalone modules have identical allocation and operations apart from the two declared selections. This adds 4*16*112=7168 dense parameters, estimated total32115429/dense322213/embedding31793216. The coarse summary can respond to block-specific mean changes; the duplicate cannot. Norm matching limits coefficient-scale confounds without asserting activation or hardware equivalence.
predictions: Primary predeclared information contrast: validation click AUC(block_task)-AUC(duplicate_task)>0; require block_task to also exceed incumbent g0-r0012-position_task (0.6635245220527689) and both frozen source bests (0.660646940486458 and 0.660163362657485) for a useful new selection.

Estimate the same information contrast in the shared cell. Compute D=[AUC(block_task)-AUC(duplicate_task)]-[AUC(block_shared)-AUC(duplicate_shared)]. Only positive, repeated D supports interaction with task conditioning; main effects alone do not establish synergy.

The new third summary is exactly zero in reference algebra for empty histories and histories restricted to one block. After training, prediction differences on those slices may still arise through globally changed learned weights; do not interpret them as direct temporal evidence.

On exploratory predeclared history slices (empty,1-16,17-64,>64), coarse information is structurally available only when multiple blocks are occupied. Report counts, positives and negatives and mark insufficient slices. Existing full validation counts are 6444/427,461684/28818,1001754/55298,1401885/50957 (samples/positives). No new host slice interface is assumed.

All four new cells have the same parameter count and operator shapes; host measured wall/GPU cost, peak memory and inference p50/p95/throughput must establish actual cost. Report all auxiliary AUCs/Logloss and auxiliary mean separately even if click improves.
falsifiers: If block_task does not beat duplicate_task, the tested coarse statistic has no supported click information advantage over this capacity-matched replacement; do not attribute an advantage over the old incumbent to chronology.

If duplicate_task explains the full gain over the incumbent, added width/reparameterization remains the leading explanation. If neither improves the incumbent, retain the incumbent and record a null or negative branch.
If D is nonpositive, fail the predicted task-conditioning interaction for this implementation even if an information main effect exists; repeated-seed uncertainty can also leave D unresolved.

If any host check finds padding sensitivity outside allowed inputs, current-action dependence, auxiliary item/scorer gradient leakage, nonfinite computation or inconsistent bank execution, the experiment is invalid until corrected; keep charged failed receipts.

If an AUC gain is not repeatable, has unresolved paired uncertainty, or is dominated on measured quality/cost, do not label it a confirmed or efficient mechanism. A positive result versus duplication still does not establish monotone chronology versus arbitrary block-coded projections; that requires a separate matched scrambled-block replacement.
